title: How Google finds your page, and the free tools to check it

say: How Google finds your page, and the free tools to check it.
This is the video for module one of the SEO course.
SEO stands for search engine optimisation.
It means making a website easier for search engines to find, understand and show to the right people, without paying for each click.

say: Stage one is crawling. Google uses automatic programs called crawlers. Google's crawler is called Googlebot.
Crawlers find new pages mainly by following links, and from sitemaps, which are files that list a site's pages.

panel.heading: Three stages every page passes
items: Crawling: Googlebot visits pages through links
Indexing: Google understands and stores the page
Serving: Google shows the most useful matches

say: Stage two is indexing. Google reads the text, headings, images and title, and may store the page in its index, a huge database of pages.
Copies, very thin pages and pages with a noindex instruction are usually left out.

panel.heading: Three stages every page passes
items: Crawling: Googlebot visits pages through links
Indexing: Google understands and stores the page
Serving: Google shows the most useful matches

say: Stage three is serving results. When someone searches, Google returns the pages it thinks are most relevant and useful.

panel.heading: Three stages every page passes
items: Crawling: Googlebot visits pages through links
Indexing: Google understands and stores the page
Serving: Google shows the most useful matches

say: So remember this. A page can only rank after it has been crawled and indexed. A problem early in the flow blocks everything after it.

panel.heading: Three stages every page passes
items: Crawling: Googlebot visits pages through links
Indexing: Google understands and stores the page
Serving: Google shows the most useful matches
panel.rule: No crawl, no index. No index, no ranking.

Ten days later the page appears

say: You can control whether your pages can be crawled, what they say, how fast and mobile friendly they are, and how your Google Business Profile looks.

panel.heading: What you can and cannot control

say: You cannot control Google's ranking systems, your competitors, or how many people search.
Nobody can guarantee a number one position. Google itself warns site owners to be careful of anyone who promises that.

panel.heading: What you can and cannot control

say: First, turn on 2-Step Verification, so a stolen password alone cannot open your Google account.

panel.heading: Set up Search Console safely
items: Turn on 2-Step Verification
Add your site in Search Console

Submit your sitemap
Add helpers as users

say: Next, go to Search Console and add your site. A Domain property covers every version of the site. A URL prefix property covers one exact address and offers more ways to verify.

say: Then open the Sitemaps report and submit your sitemap address. Chioma's took about 20 minutes in total.

say: Finally, if a designer or volunteer helps you, never share your password. Add them as a user with Full or Restricted permission, and remove their access the same day they stop working with you.

say: Small businesses get many scam messages. The first promises guaranteed number one on Google in 7 days. Google's own advice says no one can guarantee that.

cards.d: Promises of number one on Google in 7 days. No honest SEO can guarantee a top ranking.
Offers of thousands of backlinks or reviews. Buying them breaks Google's policies and can harm your site.
Emails claiming your site will be removed from Google unless you pay. Ignore them.

say: The second offers to sell thousands of backlinks or reviews. Buying them breaks Google's policies and can harm your site.

say: Tick every item before you start changing pages.
Then write down a baseline: clicks and impressions for the last 28 days, and your top five searches. Without a starting point, you cannot prove your work made a difference.

panel.heading: Safe setup checklist
items: 2-Step Verification on
Search Console verified
Sitemap submitted
Business Profile claimed
Helpers added as users
Passwords never shared

say: To remember. Google crawls, indexes, then serves. Crawlers find pages through links and sitemaps. Use the site search for a quick check. Protect your account and never share passwords. And nobody can guarantee a top position.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Google works in three stages: crawl, index, serve
Crawlers find pages through links and sitemaps
Use site:yourdomain.com for a quick index check
Turn on 2-Step Verification; never share passwords
Nobody can guarantee a top position

say: Now try it. Run a site search on a website you know, map five customer searches to their intent, then verify a site in Search Console and submit its sitemap.
